synopsis: The Minerals Council South Africa, through its MOSH learning hub, supplied engineering requirements and independent verification methods for Regulation 8.10, which specified what must be done but not how [f15636, f15638, f10458, f10856]. The Council funded a multi-million-rand project whose common requirements were published in January 2022; its compliance approach includes TRL4 and TRL7 verification gates and a fail-to-safe addendum rather than treating Gazette wording as a complete engineering specification [f10857, f2590, f2593]. Specific requirements include a minimum 200 m detection range, a Deutsch DT 12-pin connector with ISO/TS 21815-2 negotiation, and intervention logging at 10 Hz retained for seven days onboard and three months on a server [f2113, f2591, f2592]. DMRE data reported via the Council record 49 mining deaths in 2022, including 17 in the transport and mining category versus 16 in 2021; the narrower trade-press claim of only one TMM collision-related death in 2022 could not be verified in a primary source [f3199, f3200, f3142, f3145]. Trade press also attributes operator over-reliance concerns to a Council study on unintended consequences, but that study was not found, leaving the underlying evidence unavailable [f3445, f3446].
